hook.line: On the Caribbean coast everyone has an *if only*: if only it were cooler, if only we could stay another week. English handles that with a plain past tense (*I wish I had*). Spanish has its own set of forms for it, and you already know where to find them.
hook.en: I wish I could stay here.

examples.en: I wish I had more time.
I wish I could help you. (to a friend)
I wish it weren't so hot.
I wish there were more tables.
I wish I knew how to speak better.

rule:
You already use *ojalá* with the wish forms for something that could still happen: *Ojalá no llueva* (I hope it doesn't rain). When you wish for something that isn't true right now, or probably won't happen, you switch to a second set of forms.

To build it, start from the *ellos* form of the past: *tuvieron*, *pudieron*, *fueron*, *estuvieron*. Drop *ron* and add:
*ra*, *ras*, *ra*, *ramos*, *ran*

*tuvieron* becomes *tuviera*, *tuvieras*, *tuviera*, *tuviéramos*, *tuvieran*.

The *nosotros* form gets an accent on the vowel before *ramos*: *pudiéramos*, *estuviéramos*.

So *Ojalá tengas tiempo* is a hope (maybe you will), and *Ojalá tuvieras tiempo* is a wish (you don't). English only changes the tense; Spanish changes the form, and it works for every verb.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect subjunctive (*imperfecto de subjuntivo*). You will also see an *se* version, *tuviese*, *pudiese*, in books. It means the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *tenga* or *tuviera* and type the whole sentence: *Ojalá ___ más tiempo.* (I wish I had more time, but I don't.)
yourTurn.why: You are wishing for something that isn't true, so you need the second set of forms: *tuviera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *pueda* or *pudiera* and type the whole sentence: *Ojalá ___ ayudarte.* (I wish I could help you, but I can't. To a friend.)
yourTurn.why: *Pudiera* comes from *pudieron*, and it is the form for a wish that isn't true.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wish it were easier.
Type in Spanish: I wish Vale were here.
yourTurn.why: *Estuvieron* becomes *estuviera*; it is the same ending for *yo* and for *ella*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wish we could stay.
yourTurn.why: For *nosotros* it is *pudiéramos*, with the accent on the vowel before *ramos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the hope into a wish. It is a very hot day and there is no hope: *Ojalá haga menos calor.*
yourTurn.why: *Hicieron* gives *hiciera*; the wish form changes to the second set.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a friend instead: *Ojalá tuviera un carro.* (I wish you had a car.)

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tuve* just reports something that happened; a wish needs the *ra* form.
English copies its past tense here (*I wish I had*), but Spanish needs the special form, not the ordinary past.
Start from *tuvieron*, not from the infinitive: the irregular stem carries over.
For *nosotros* the stress moves, so the accent goes on the vowel before *ramos*.

personal: Say one thing you wish were different, starting with *Ojalá*: *Ojalá pudiera…*, *Ojalá tuviera…*, *Ojalá fuera…*. Something true about you, right now.
